shortDescription: By Emmanuel BruceGhana will open its 2026/27 cocoa season on Friday, five sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

children: Ghana will open its 2026/27 cocoa season on Friday, five sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
The finance ministry is expected to announce the new season as well as the farmgate price, the sources said.

Ghana and Ivory Coast, the world's two biggest cocoa producers, agreed in June to harmonise farmgate prices and season start dates following a meeting between the two countries’ presidents. But Ivory Coast opened its season on September 1.

The Chamber of Cocoa Marketers, which represents licensed buyers, last week said sector regulator COCOBOD still owes its members 4 billion cedis ($349 million) for cocoa purchased last season, warning that financing may not yet be in place to fund purchases once the season opens.
COCOBOD is seeking to raise 16.3 billion cedis from domestic investors through commercial paper and bonds, turning to the local capital market to fund cocoa purchases, Reuters reported this week.
COCOBOD said this week its management had held meetings with leaders of farmer associations, executives of the Chamber of Cocoa Marketers and international trading partners ahead of the new season.
